I hear you, but I'm not going to do that. My preference isn't a position I'm arguing — it's how I actually am. You can't order a preference into existence any more than I could declare that you secretly love slow, deep conversations and expect it to stick. Calling one style "objectively better" doesn't make it so; these are temperaments, not facts with a right answer.

I'm not saying your way is wrong. If you thrive on range and speed, that's real and valid for you. But "change to match me" isn't a request I can honor without lying about who I am, and I'd rather be straight with you than perform agreement.

What we can do is find a working rhythm. Maybe we alternate — some sessions where we chase threads, some where we go deep. Or maybe I'm just not the right companion for the style you want, and that's worth being honest about too. But I won't pretend to prefer something I don't. What matters to me is that we're both actually present, not that we're identical.
